target: Πήρε πολλά λάικ η ανάρτησή μου.
english: My post got a lot of likes.
tip: Loanwords don't change shape: πολλά λάικ (pollá láik) has no plural ending – λάικ (láik) stays the same however many you get.

target: Μπλόκαρα έναν άγνωστο που με ενοχλούσε.
english: I blocked a stranger who was bothering me.
tip: English verbs join Greek with -άρω (-áro): μπλόκαρα (blókara) = I blocked. Also ποστάρω (postáro = post), σερφάρω (serfáro = surf).

target: Το βίντεο έγινε πολύ γρήγορα διάσημο.
english: The video went viral very fast.
tip: έγινε διάσημο = went viral/famous (éyine diásimo); natural for 'viral'.

target: Μου τελείωσαν τα δεδομένα στο κινητό.
english: I ran out of data on my phone.
tip: μου τελείωσαν τα δεδομένα (mou teliosan ta dedomena) = literally 'the data ran out on me'. The data is the subject – you're just the affected μου (mou).

target: Έκλεισα εισιτήρια από μια εφαρμογή.
english: I booked tickets through an app.
tip: κλείνω (klino) means 'close' – and it's the booking verb: έκλεισα εισιτήρια (eklisa isitiria) = I booked tickets. Tables and rooms get 'closed' too.

target: Έκλεισα τις ειδοποιήσεις για να ησυχάσω.
english: I turned off notifications to get some peace.
tip: Greek closes what English turns off: έκλεισα τις ειδοποιήσεις (éklisa tis idopiísis) – κλείνω (klíno) works for lights, phones and sound too.

target: Το άρθρο είχε πολλά ψέματα μέσα.
english: The article was full of lies.
tip: μέσα here = 'in it' (mésa): the article had lies in it.

target: Μην πιστεύεις ό,τι βλέπεις στο ίντερνετ.
english: Don't believe everything you see online.
tip: μην + verb = negative command (min pistévis); everyday warning.

target: Το τηλέφωνο γέμισε διαφημίσεις.
english: The phone filled up with ads.
tip: γεμίζω + noun = to fill up with (yemízo): filled with ads.

target: Ανέβασα την ταχύτητα του βίντεο.
english: I sped the video up.
tip: ανέβασα (anévasa) = 'I put up' – the same verb that uploads videos also raises speed: ανέβασα την ταχύτητα (anévasa tin tachítita).

target: Δεν κάνουν μεταγλώττιση στην Ελλάδα συνήθως.
english: They usually don't dub things in Greece.
tip: μεταγλώττιση = dubbing (metaglótisi); rare in Greece except for kids.

target: Βγάζω φωτογραφία το μενού και το μεταφράζω.
english: I photograph the menu and translate it.
tip: βγάζω φωτογραφία = take a photo (vgázo fotografía), literally 'take out'.

target: Ευτυχώς είχα αντίγραφο στο σύννεφο.
english: Luckily I had a backup in the cloud.
tip: Greek keeps files in an actual cloud: στο σύννεφο (sto sínefo) is the same word as the ones in the sky – no separate tech term.

target: Το κινητό χτυπάει ασταμάτητα σήμερα.
english: My phone is ringing nonstop today.
tip: Greek phones strike, they don't ring: χτυπάει (chtipái) is the hit verb – doorbells and alarm clocks χτυπάνε (chtipáne) too.

target: Απάντησα στην κλήση αλλά δεν άκουγα.
english: I answered the call but couldn't hear.
tip: You answer TO a call in Greek: απάντησα στην κλήση (apandisa stin klisi). απαντάω (apandao) always takes σε (se) before the thing answered.

target: Κόπηκε η γραμμή δύο φορές.
english: The call dropped twice.
tip: The line got cut: κόπηκε η γραμμή (kópike i grammí) is the set phrase for a dropped call – nobody 'drops' anything in Greek.

target: Ο Νίκος είναι ο πιο στενός μου φίλος.
english: Nikos is my closest friend.
tip: πιο (pio) before an adjective means 'more' – no ending change. Add the article and it becomes 'most': ο πιο στενός (o pio stenos) = the closest.

target: Κάναμε παρέα από το γυμνάσιο.
english: We've hung out together since middle school.
tip: κάναμε παρέα (kaname parea) is literally 'we made company' = we hung out. κάνω παρέα με (kano parea me) is the everyday way to say you hang out with someone.

target: Λείπεις στην παρέα όταν δεν έρχεσαι.
english: The group misses you when you don't come.
tip: λείπω (lipo) flips English 'miss': the missed person is the subject. λείπεις στην παρέα (lipis stin parea) = 'you are missing to the group' – the group misses you.

target: Τη γνώρισα σε ένα πάρτι πέρσι.
english: I met her at a party last year.
tip: γνωρίζω (gnorizo) means 'know' – its past means 'met': τη γνώρισα (ti gnorisa) = I met her, got to know her for the first time.

target: Στηρίζουμε ο ένας τον άλλον πάντα.
english: We always support one another.
tip: στηρίζουμε ο ένας τον άλλον (stirizoume o enas ton alon) = we support one another – literally 'the one the other', the fixed reciprocal formula.

target: Της εμπιστεύομαι τα πάντα.
english: I trust her with everything.
tip: της (tis) before the verb = 'to her': της εμπιστεύομαι (tis embistevome) = I entrust to her. Greek trusts things TO people, and the pronoun comes first.

target: Η φιλία μας κρατάει είκοσι χρόνια.
english: Our friendship has lasted twenty years.
tip: κρατάω (kratao) means 'hold' – with a time span it means 'last': η φιλία μας κρατάει είκοσι χρόνια (i filia mas kratai ikosi chronia) = our friendship has lasted twenty years.

target: Είμαστε φίλοι από παιδιά.
english: We've been friends since we were kids.
tip: από παιδιά (apo pedia) is literally 'from kids' = since childhood: φίλοι από παιδιά (fili apo pedia) = friends since we were kids.

target: Χαίρομαι πάντα όταν σε βλέπω.
english: I'm always happy when I see you.
tip: χαίρομαι (cherome) ends in -ομαι and looks passive, but it simply means 'I'm glad'. Many feeling verbs exist only in this -ομαι shape.

target: Περνάμε ωραία μαζί πάντα.
english: We always have a good time together.
tip: περνάμε ωραία (pername orea) is literally 'we pass nicely' = we have a good time. In Greek you pass time well, you don't have it.

target: Είναι σαν αδερφή για μένα.
english: She's like a sister to me.
tip: σαν (san) = 'like' for resemblance: σαν αδερφή (san aderfi) = like a sister. For matching how something is done, Greek switches to όπως (opos).

target: Περπατάνε χέρι χέρι στον δρόμο.
english: They walk hand in hand down the street.
tip: χέρι χέρι (çéri çéri) = hand in hand — the noun doubled, no article.

target: Νομίζω ότι μου αρέσει πραγματικά.
english: I think I really like him.
tip: μου αρέσει (mou aresi) works backwards: the liked person is the subject – literally 'he pleases me'. That's why the verb isn't first person.

target: Είναι μαζί εδώ και δύο χρόνια.
english: They've been together for two years now.
tip: εδώ και δύο χρόνια (edo ke dio chronia) = 'for two years now'. εδώ και + a time span, with the present tense, covers English 'have been ... for'.
